summary: Contestants demonstrate their knowledge of computer networking concepts, including network design, configuration, hardware, protocols, and security. The event includes an objective test and, at Nationals, a certification exam and a hands-on final round for top contestants. Both secondary and postsecondary students may participate individually.
time_limits: Preliminaries - No more than sixty (60) minutes for objective test
Preliminaries (Nationals only) - sixty (60) minutes for objective test, no more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test, and no more than sixty (60) minutes for performance component
Finals (Nationals only) - No more than sixty (60) minutes for performance component
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
(Optional) Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards
competencies: Design, configure, and troubleshoot computer networks using OSI/TCP-IP models, subnetting, and IPv4/IPv6 addressing to ensure scalable and secure connectivity
Install, configure, and troubleshoot computer hardware components to ensure reliable performance and minimize downtime in networked environments
Configure and manage core network services including DNS, DHCP, etc. to enable efficient name resolution, addressing, and resource discovery
Deploy and manage cloud, virtualization, and secure remote-access technologies to support scalable and hybrid network infrastructures
Administer directory services and operating systems to ensure secure authentication, centralized management, and efficient enterprise operations
Identify key features of Wi-Fi 6/6E/7, explain how they improve network efficiency and performance, and describe appropriate use cases for modern wireless deployments
Compare cloud networking models and explain how networking, security, and access controls differ between public, private, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
Explain how SD-WAN functions, identify its advantages over traditional WANs, and describe how SD-WAN improves application performance and network reliability
Define zero-trust networking, explain its core principles, and describe how it is implemented to secure modern enterprise networks
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed

Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
At NLC, contestants will take IT Specialist Networking certification as part of the event. Contestants passing this certification will have 50 points added to their event score.
A Pearson profile must be created at https://certiport.pearsonvue.com before attending NLC
Contestants must include their BPA Contestant ID in their Pearson profile when they register
Certiport Parent/Legal Guardian Consent Form must be uploaded to: education@bpa.org
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing

The top 10 contestants at Nationals will advance to a final round that includes a hands-on component. Scores from the preliminary round and the objective test will not carry over to the finals. Reference materials may be used during the application portion of the final round.
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this objective event.
